answer.appeal_deadline: 180 days from the date of the notice (2026-08-04), i.e., must be received by 2027-01-31, per the denial letter itself.
answer.submission_route: The denial letter references an internal appeal right but the excerpt provided does not include a specific mailing address or portal for this member's plan. UnitedHealthcare's generic commercial member appeals address is: UnitedHealthCare Member Inquiry/Appeals, PO Box 30432, Salt Lake City, UT 84130-0432. Members can also typically file appeals online through myuhc.com (member portal) or by calling the member services number on the back of the insurance ID card, which will route to Iowa-specific appeals handling. The full, official denial letter (of which only an excerpt was provided here) should contain the exact mailing address, fax number, and/or online submission link specific to Emerson Brooks's plan — that address on the actual notice should be used rather than the generic one, since ACA/Iowa-specific appeal units can differ.
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The UnitedHealthcare 'Surgery of the Shoulder' policy does not itself contain the substantive medical-necessity clinical criteria for CPT 23472. Instead, it incorporates by reference a proprietary, licensed clinical decision-support product — InterQual® CP: Procedures, 'Joint Replacement, Shoulder' (and, if revision surgery, 'Removal and Replacement or Revision, Joint Replacement, Shoulder') — which is not freely published online; access requires an InterQual license (typically held by UHC and its reviewers) or the specific InterQual excerpt UHC is required to release to the member/provider upon request. Under ERISA/ACA claims-procedure regulations and most state insurance codes (including Iowa's), the patient or provider has the right to request, free of charge, the specific internal rule, guideline, or criterion relied upon in denying the claim. The patient should: (1) call the member services number on the ID card or write to the appeals address on the denial notice and explicitly request 'a copy of the specific InterQual criteria (Joint Replacement, Shoulder) applied to this denial, plus any internal medical necessity guideline used,' citing the reference number POC-9AB63CFCDF-18778; and (2) ask the treating orthopedic surgeon's office to request the same directly from UHC's Provider Services/Medical Director, since providers can often obtain the InterQual criteria sheet used in the review through a peer-to-peer consultation.
answer.notes: High confidence that 'Surgery of the Shoulder' (Commercial/Individual Exchange Medical Policy) is the correct governing UHC policy for CPT 23472 in a commercial/ACA Iowa plan — CPT 23472 is explicitly listed in its Applicable Codes table and no separate UHC commercial policy specifically for total shoulder arthroplasty was found. However, confidence is only medium-to-low regarding whether the *exact* posted version (Policy Number 2026T0556GG, effective 09/01/2026) was the version in force on the notice date of 2026-08-04, since UHC revises and renumbers this policy periodically and only the current version is posted publicly; older superseded versions are generally not available at the public URL. More importantly, this UHC policy is a 'router' document — the actual medical-necessity checklist (symptom severity, imaging findings, failed conservative treatment duration, etc.) lives in InterQual® CP 'Joint Replacement, Shoulder,' a copyrighted, licensed criteria set that is NOT publicly posted by UnitedHealthcare or the InterQual vendor (Change Healthcare/Optum). I could not retrieve the text of those InterQual criteria; only third-party payers' own paraphrased summaries of similar (but not necessarily identical or current) InterQual shoulder-replacement criteria exist online (e.g., Providence Health Plan, BCBS Michigan), and these should not be assumed to be identical to the version UHC applied. The patient's appeal should explicitly demand the specific InterQual criteria pages used in this determination, since the incomplete-documentation denial reason suggests the reviewer could not confirm specific InterQual data elements (e.g., failed conservative treatment history, imaging findings, functional limitation measures) were present in the submitted records.
